plan.english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, grow light!

notes: Ved. uṣo ví ucha duhitar divaḥ 'Dawn, shine forth, daughter of Heaven' (RV 1.48.1), the vocative of the title; Greek has the vocative Διὸς θύγατερ (to Aphrodite, Il. 5.348) and of Eos only δῖα < *diw-yā 'of Zeus' (Od. 9.151); West reconstructs pre-Homeric *Diwós tʰugátēr of Dawn. Interpolated: the verb, the -sḱé- present of *h₂wes- 'become light' (Ved. ucchati; Lith. aušta 'it dawns' is the same root but not in a cited passage). Lith. Diẽvo is *deywós (Diẽvas 'god'), not *dyḗws: the Baltic ref supports dʰugh₂tḗr only (dukrýtė, a diminutive of duktė̃), not diwés. RV 1.48.1, Il. 5.348 and Od. 9.151 checked in the local corpora; Rhesa is not in local corpora. The builder's reflex table has no key for Ved. duhitár- or Gk ἠώς, so secure_checks undercount those two.

The dawn is a birth: Ved. uṣáso jā́yamānāḥ 'the Dawns as they are born' (RV 6.52.4) and Homer's Eos ἠριγένεια 'early-born', who φάνη 'appeared' (Il. 1.477); both checked locally. ǵenh₁- is shared only at root level (Ved. jā́yamāna-, a -ye- present; Gk -γένεια in a compound); the participle uses the reduplicated present middle, which neither branch has. Revised: 'shine' had been taken from another hymn (RV 6.65.2 bhānty uṣásaḥ, now support only); in the parallel pair it is Greek only (φάνη, the n-present aorist of *bʰeh₂-), so the verb is interpolated. The Vedic plural 'Dawns' is kept.

Ved. úṣo ... ví bhāhi 'Dawn, shine forth' (RV 3.61.2) and Homeric φάε ... Ἠώς 'Dawn shone' (Od. 14.502; φάω from *bʰeh₂-), both checked locally. The Greek is a 3rd-person past, the Vedic an imperative: the mood follows the Vedic. Ved. ví 'forth' has no lexeme. Revised from 'Dawn, immortal one, shine!': Ved. ámartyā (3.61.2) is *-t-yo-, not *n̥mr̥tós, amŕ̥tā stands in another hymn (1.113.13), and Bacchylides' ἄμβροτος is not in a local corpus, so 'immortal' is dropped (it also came out as the engine's feminine eh₂-stem vocative ń̥mr̥teh₂, identical to the nominative, an engine issue not fixable in a plan).

Ved. yukṣvá ... áśvān ... uṣaḥ 'yoke the (red) horses, Dawn' (RV 1.92.15); in the Odyssey Athena holds back Dawn and does not let her yoke (ζεύγνυσθ’) her swift-footed horses (Od. 23.244–246); both checked locally. Revised to the middle, which both branches have (Ved. yukṣvá, s-aorist middle imperative; Gk ζεύγνυσθαι, nasal-present middle): the s-aorist middle imperative follows the Vedic. The stems differ (Vedic s-aorist, Greek -νυ- present), so *yewg- is shared at root level as to formation, and the Greek is negated narrative, not a command. Ved. aruṇā́n 'red' and Gk ὠκύποδας 'swift-footed' differ and are left out.

Dawn rises 'to bring light' (Il. 11.1–2 ἠὼς ... ὄρνυθ’ ἵν’ ... φόως φέροι) and the Vedic Dawns are jyótir bhárantīḥ 'bringing light' (RV 10.35.5, one pāda); both checked locally. *bʰer- and the Dawn are shared; the object follows Gk φόως (*bʰéh₂-os; Ved. jyótis- is another word): interpolated. The Vedic participle and the Greek optative are rendered as a present. Revised: 'to mortals' had been stitched on from another hymn (RV 6.65.3 mártyāya; Ved. mártya- is *mr̥t-yo-, Gk βροτοῖσι *mr̥tó-) and is dropped.

Vedic Dawn 'has been seen' (uṣā́ adarśi, RV 7.77.3; práty adr̥śran, 7.78.3) and is darśatā́ 'a sight to behold'; Hesiod's Dawn is πολυδερκής 'much-seeing' (Th. 451, cited from West 2007 ch. 5), the same root *derḱ-. The Vedic aorist passive is rendered with the middle aorist. Root-level only: Hesiod has the root in a compound with the opposite diathesis ('much-seeing' against Vedic 'was seen'), and West 2007 ch. 5 presents only a root association. RV 7.77.3 and 7.78.3 checked locally; Hesiod is not in local corpora.

Ved. urviyā́ ví bhāti 'she shines out widely' (RV 1.92.9; 6.64.2, of Uṣas) has the elements of the Greek name Εὐρυφάεσσα (εὐρυ- + φα-, Hymn. Hom. 31.2), which Campanile derives from a formula *'broad-shining Dawn' (West 2007 ch. 5). Ved. urviyā́ is an instrumental of urú- used as an adverb: rendered as the instrumental neuter of h₁wérHus. In the hymn Euryphaessa has become Dawn's mother (Eos is named at 31.6), so h₂éwsōs as the one who shines widely is Vedic only and is not counted as secure. Εὐρυφάεσσα is a proper name, so the Greek supports the line only as a name and at root level; the wording rests on Vedic urviyā́ ... bhāti (RV 1.92.9, 6.64.2, both checked). The Homeric Hymn is not in local corpora.

plan.english: The shining Dawns gave birth to the Sun.

notes: Ved. uṣáso vibhātī́r ájījanan sū́ryam 'the shining Dawns have given birth to the Sun' (RV 7.78.3). In Greek the Sun's mother is Theia, who 'bore great Helios ... and Eos' (Hes. Th. 371–374), or Euryphaessa 'broad-shining' (Hymn. Hom. 31.2), whom West takes to be Dawn herself forgotten as such. Shared: ǵenh₁- (ájījanan, γείνατο), the Sun, and *bʰeh₂- 'shine' (vibhātī́ḥ, -φάεσσα). h₂éwsōs as mother is Vedic only: interpolated. The Hesiodic forms are cited from the standard text, not verifiable locally (West quotes Th. 371 Ἠέλιόν τε μέγαν). Revised: Euryphaessa (a name) is support only, and *bʰeh₂- 'shine' (vibhātī́ḥ against the name -φάεσσα) is no longer claimed. In the Greek parallel the mother is Theia, so only 'bore the Sun' is shared (Ved. ájījanan, reduplicated aorist; Gk γείνατο: ǵenh₁- at root level). RV 7.78.3 checked; Hesiod and the Hymn are not in local corpora.

West 2007 ch. 5: 'the Sun, like Dyaus/Zeus, has the epithet great ... the Vedic and Greek adjectives are cognate' (RV 3.2.7 súvar mahát, with the neuter sun word like PIE *sóh₂wl̥; RV 2.23.2 Sū́riyo ... mahó, whose construal is uncertain, support; Hes. Th. 19 and 371 Ἠέλιόν τε μέγαν). Copula removed: the daughters have an attributive phrase at RV 3.2.7 (svàr mahát, object of ā́ ... apr̥ṇat) and Hes. Th. 19 (Ἠέλιόν τε μέγαν, in a catalogue of gods), not a predication, so the line is the noun phrase. Revised: 'up goes' came from RV 7.63.2, where mahā́n goes with ketúḥ 'banner', not with the Sun; dropped. RV 3.2.7 and 2.23.2 checked locally; Hesiod is not in local corpora. Gk ἠέλιος has no key in the builder's reflex table.

The Sun is 'swift' with cognate adjectives: AV 13.2.2 āśúm ... sū́ryam, Mimnermus ὠκέος Ἠελίοιο (fr. 11a.1, 14.11); both cited from West 2007 ch. 5 (no local corpus). The verb *bʰeh₂- 'shine' is interpolated.

Helios is θεῶν σκοπὸν ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν 'watcher of gods and men' (Hymn. Dem. 62; not in local corpora); Sūrya is spáśaṃ víśvasya jágataḥ 'spy of all that moves' (RV 4.13.3, checked). Ved. spáś- = *spéḱs; Gk σκοπός is an o-grade thematic derivative of the same root, so the head is shared at root level only (not 'Kuhn's equation'). Copula removed: the daughters have apposition at RV 4.13.3 (táṃ sū́ryaṃ ... spáśam, objects of vahanti) and Hymn. Hom. Dem. 62 (Ἠέλιον ... σκοπόν), so the line is a noun phrase with the watcher in apposition to the Sun. Revised: the genitives 'of gods and men' were dropped: they have no counterpart in RV 4.13.3, and h₂nḗr had been verified through the compound nr̥cákṣas- of another hymn (RV 7.60.2).

plan.english: The Sun goes up for mortals.

notes: The Sun rising for mortals: 'this Sūrya goes up (út eti) ... (looking at) the straight and the crooked among mortals (márteṣu)' (RV 7.60.2) and Helios 'leapt up' (ἀνόρουσε) to shine for the immortals and for mortal men (βροτοῖσιν, Od. 3.1–3); West 2007 ch. 5 pairs the Greek with Vedic sunrise passages. Both checked locally. Ved. márta- = Gk βροτός (*mr̥tós). The case follows the Greek dative (with φαείνοι 'to shine for'); the Vedic has the locative with páśyan. 'Goes up' (úd + h₁ey-) is Vedic; ἀνόρουσε is another verb: interpolated. Revised: the participle 'looking at' (páśyan, root-matched to σκοπός from the Hymn to Demeter, another text) and 'over the earth' (Ved. jmán only) are dropped. The builder's reflex table has no key for Ved. márta-.

Ved. sū́ra úditaḥ vibhā́ti 'the Sun, risen, shines forth' (RV 10.121.6c); Zeus to Helios: Ἠέλι’ ... φάεινε 'Helios, shine' (Od. 12.385, which West 2007 ch. 5 cites beside Od. 3.1–3). Both checked locally. *bʰeh₂- is shared at root level (Ved. bhā́ti, root present; Gk φαείνω, a derived present); the indicative follows the Vedic. Revised: the participle 'going up' (Ved. úd-ita-, a past participle; the Greek has another verb) was interpolated and is dropped, and the Greek locus is now Od. 12.385 so that this line does not share Od. 3.1–3 with dawn-sun-012.

theme: The Sun's motion: wheel and steeds (West 2007 ch. 5)
notes: The Sun's wheel: Ved. cakrám of Sūrya (eleven times; RV 2.11.20 'as Sūrya sets his wheel rolling', ávartayat), Greek ἡλίου κύκλος (Aesch. Pers. 504 etc.; Eur. El. 464f., cited from West 2007 ch. 5), and in the Edda the elves call the sun fagrahvél 'fair wheel' (Alvíssmál 16, beside sól and sunna). All three continue *kʷékʷlos and *sóh₂wl̥ (Gk ἥλιος from *seh₂wel-iyos). Interpolated: the causative wortéye- 'turn' (Ved. vartáya-, Vedic only in these passages); present for the habitual.

theme: The Sun's motion: wheel and steeds (West 2007 ch. 5)

plan.english: The horse draws the wheel of the Sun.

notes: 'The wheel of Sūrya that Etaśa draws (váhati), yoked in harness' (RV 7.63.2); 'one horse draws' the one-wheeled car (1.164.2); Euripides' shield shows 'the Sun's shining wheel on winged mares' (El. 464f., from West 2007 ch. 5), which West reads as the old horse-drawn wheel. Interpolated: wéǵʰe- 'draw, convey' (Ved. váhati only). West notes the horse-and-wheel image need not be Proto-Indo-European in date. Revised: RV 1.164.2 (a riddle hymn, another passage) is support only. In RV 7.63.2 the drawer is Etaśa, the Sun's horse by name, so h₁éḱwos is Greek (ἵπποις) only and interpolated. RV 7.63.2 and 1.164.2 checked; Euripides is not in local corpora.

theme: The Sun's motion: wheel and steeds (West 2007 ch. 5)

plan.english: The horses of the Sun have taken their stand in the sky.

notes: 'The bay horses of Sūrya ... have mounted the back of heaven' (RV 1.115.3, diváḥ ... pr̥ṣṭhám asthuḥ); the goddesses find Helios before his horses (Hymn. Dem. 62f.); the Avestan Sun is 'swift-horsed' (Y. 16.4). Ved. pr̥ṣṭhá- 'back' has no usable lexeme; 'in the sky' (locative of *dyḗws) and the aorist of steh₂- (Ved. asthuḥ) are interpolated. Hymn. Dem. 63 ἵππων is cited from the standard text, not verifiable locally.

plan.english: The Sun, the eye of Sky.

notes: Macrobius reports that 'antiquity' called the sun Iouis oculus; the sun and moon are 'the two eyes of Dyaus' (RV 1.72.10, divó ... akṣī́), lexically = Διὸς ὄσσε (Il. 14.286); West 2007 ch. 4 n. 25, ch. 5. Interpolated: *sóh₂wl̥ as subject (Latin sol in Macrobius' context only; Vedic has no sun word in the stanza). Copula removed: the daughters have a genitive phrase, not a predication (RV 1.72.10 divó ... akṣī́, object of ákr̥ṇvan; Il. 14.286 Διὸς ὄσσε, object; Macrobius' Iouis oculus, named with appellat), so the line is a noun phrase with the eye in apposition to the Sun (Macrobius' equation). Revised: Il. 14.286 is support only: Διὸς ὄσσε there are Zeus' own eyes, and West 2007 ch. 4 n. 25 says the phrase matches divó akṣī́ 'etymologically, though not semantically'. RV 1.72.10 and Il. 14.286 checked locally; Macrobius is not in local corpora.

theme: The Daughter of the Sun (West 2007 ch. 5)

plan.english: The daughter of the Sun stood on the chariot.

notes: Ved. duhitā́ sū́ryasya 'the daughter of the Sun' mounts the Aśvins' chariot (RV 1.116.17, ā́ ... rátham ... atiṣṭhat); Lith. Sáulės dukrýtė / Sáules dukte, a byword for a paragon (Brodowski, in Mannhardt 1936: 614; West 2007 ch. 5). Lith. saulė is *seh₂ul-yeh₂, a derivative of the sun word. Interpolated: the chariot (Hroth₂ós, Ved. rátha-) and the aorist of steh₂- (Ved. atiṣṭhat is an imperfect).

plan.english: The many cows of the Sun.

notes: The Sun's cattle: 'there many cattle of Helios graze' (Od. 12.127–128; the 350 cows of the year, West 2007 ch. 5). In RV 7.36.1 the 'cows' the Sun releases with his rays (ví raśmíbhiḥ sasr̥je sū́ryo gā́ḥ) are the rays or dawns, not a herd: the Vedic shares the words (sū́rya-, gáv-) but not the image. Both loci checked locally. Interpolated: polh₁ús 'many' (Gk πολλαί only). Copula removed: the daughters have an attributive phrase, not a predication (Od. 12.127–128 πολλαὶ ... Ἠελίοιο βόες, subject of βόσκοντ'; RV 7.36.1 gā́ḥ, object of sasr̥je), so the line is the noun phrase.

plan.english: May we live and see the Sun.

notes: To live is to see the sun: Ved. jīváse sū́ryaṃ dr̥śé 'to live, to see the Sun' (RV 10.57.4) and Homer ζώει καὶ ὁρᾷ φάος ἠελίοιο 'lives and sees the light of the sun' (Il. 18.61). Shared: *gʷih₃w- at root level (Ved. jīv-; Gk ζώει, another present formation) and the Sun. 'See' differs (Ved. dr̥śé from *derḱ-, Gk ὁρᾷ another root): *derḱ- follows the Vedic, interpolated. Revised: Il. 1.88 (ζῶντος καὶ ... δερκομένοιο, without the sun) and RV 10.37.7 (jīvā́ḥ ... paśyema, the optative wish the line follows, with spaś-) are support only. All four loci checked locally.

theme: The Sun's motion: wheel and steeds (West 2007 ch. 5)

plan.english: He drives on the great path.

notes: Ved. mahó ájmasya 'the great drive' (RV 4.53.4, of Savitr̥'s course, checked) = Gk μέγας ὄγμος (Hymn. Hom. 32.11, the Moon's orbit; not in local corpora); West 2007 ch. 5 calls it an exact equivalent (cf. Watkins 1995: 16). Ved. ájma- (*h₂éǵ-mn̥) and Gk ὄγμος (*h₂óǵ-mos) are different formations of one root, so the head is root-level. Interpolated: the verb h₂eǵ- 'drive' (the root of both nouns; the Vedic has rājati 'rules over' with the genitive) and the locative. Revised: the subject 'the Sun' (Vedic Savitr̥, Greek the Moon) was interpolated and is dropped (3rd sg. pro-drop).
